title: fix(update): retry released coordinator locks before admission
body:
## What Problem This Solves

A managed-update writer can fail admission with `sidecar changed during reclaim policy callback` when the lock holder releases normally while the reclaim policy is running. The coordinator simplification in #168859 removed the bounded retry for that release case. The contention fixture also hid later child stdout failures, making this path harder to diagnose.

Restore the retry only after a completed reclaim callback, that exact fs-safe mismatch, and an absent sidecar. Reuse the same root and original deadline before admitting caller work or SQL. An exhausted budget reports `file_lock_timeout`; surviving replacements, changed authority/root, callback failures, and unrelated errors remain fatal. Also retain bounded stdout and stderr from each fixture child using the existing 128 KiB helper, without changing synchronization, assertions, timeouts, or cleanup.

## Evidence

Focused proof uses the unchanged reviewed files:

| Test | Result | Vitest time |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `src/infra/file-lock-sync.test.ts` | 5 passed | 29.28 s |
| `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-contention.test.ts` | 2 passed | 14.91 s |
| `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-database-contention.test.ts` | 4 passed | 193.31 s |

With the same five lock tests and only the production helper reverted, normal release and deadline exhaustion fail while the three authority/replacement cases pass (16.45 s). Every candidate run finished at its expected head with no remaining child processes. Commands were `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`; the long database-contention run spent most of its time transforming modules. Both source patches received independent Codex reviews with no actionable findings. [CI run 38298120555](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38298120555) passed build, types, lint, Knip, Madge, source-contract, worker/T1 and dialect checks with these exact files. This is composition evidence, not a claim that its overall result belongs to this patch.

The published-driver × candidate update cell passed in [run 38302535736](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38302535736/job/114997195168) at composition `0541825127741ce994bdab82ff536d90444af1b9` (11m43s job, 10m46s update step). The lock and audited updater production inputs match this PR; later standalone-repair guidance and unrelated dependency refreshes are disclosed drift, not a claim of latest-main package equivalence. The scheduled Gateway log showed the same fs-safe error but did not establish whether its sidecar disappeared or was replaced; the causal proof establishes the normal-release contract without claiming the entire scheduled incident is resolved.

Scope: three files, +158/−93 lines. No authority check is removed, no transaction is replayed, and no schema, dependency, SDK, SQLite statement, or worker-request surface changes. This retries normal release inside the existing admission budget; surviving changed locks still fail.

All three final publication file blobs exactly match their reviewed sources on the current updater base. Direct-main pushes were refused by the repository ruleset, so this emergency repair uses the authorized head-pinned PR squash fallback.

Exact PR [CI run 38301514343](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38301514343) passed all applicable static gates. Its only failed test leaf was the unchanged `src/infra/update-repair-agent.e2e.test.ts`: three repair entry points abort with `Runtime config is not prepared`. The repair environment clears the snapshot and inference then calls its prepared-only reader without preparation, an independent migration gap introduced by #169714. The ten relevant test, repair-runtime, requester-authority, and config-owner files are identical across this PR, its base, and the sampled scheduled-main head. This is source attribution; the same E2E failure has not been observed in retained scheduled-main execution. A separate two-file owner repair is being validated. The lock tests and their security/authority controls pass as shown above.
